verses.text: Let as many as are bondservants under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honor, that the name of God and the doctrine not be blasphemed.

Those who have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brothers, but rather let them serve them, because those who partake of the benefit are believing and beloved. Teach and exhort these things.
If anyone teaches a different doctrine, and doesn’t consent to sound words, the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which is according to godliness,
he is conceited, knowing nothing, but obsessed with arguments, disputes, and word battles, from which come envy, strife, insulting, evil suspicions,
constant friction of people of corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who suppose that godliness is a means of gain. Withdraw yourself from such.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out.
But having food and clothing, we will be content with that.
But those who are determined to be rich fall into a temptation and a snare and many foolish and harmful lusts, such as drown men in ruin and destruction.
For the love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Some have been led astray from the faith in their greed, and have pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
But you, man of God, flee these things, and follow after righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of the eternal life to which you were called, and you confessed the good confession in the sight of many witnesses.
I command you before God, who gives life to all things, and before Christ Jesus, who before Pontius Pilate testified the good confession,
that you keep the commandment without spot, blameless, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ;
which in its own times he will show, who is the blessed and only Ruler, the King of kings, and Lord of lords;
who alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light; whom no man has seen, nor can see: to whom be honor and eternal power. Amen.
Charge those who are rich in this present world that they not be haughty, nor have their hope set on the uncertainty of riches, but on the living God, who richly provides us with everything to enjoy;
that they do good, that they be rich in good works, that they be ready to distribute, willing to communicate;
laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold of eternal life.
Timothy, guard that which is committed to you, turning away from the empty chatter and oppositions of what is falsely called knowledge;
which some profess, and thus have wandered from the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.

footnotes.content: Bondservants were to honor their masters so God's name wouldn't be blasphemed. Our witness matters in the workplace and at home. Even in unfair situations, our conduct can point others to Jesus.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: If your master is a believer, don't take advantage — serve all the more out of love. Family in Christ should make service more joyful, not less. Brotherhood changes everything.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Anyone who teaches differently and doesn't agree with Jesus' sound words is proud and ignorant. The test is simple: does it lead to godliness? If not, we should be wary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pride loves to argue about words. It breeds envy, strife, and suspicion. The cure is humility — knowing we need Jesus as much as anyone else.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some see godliness as a way to get rich. That's a tragic twist of the gospel. True godliness is about knowing and loving God, not using him. We must walk away from that mindset.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Godliness with contentment is great gain. We already have everything we need in Jesus. Contentment isn't settling — it's rejoicing in the greatest gift of all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: We came empty-handed and we'll leave the same way. That puts things in perspective. Our treasures are meant to be in heaven, not in our hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Food and clothing are enough if we have Jesus. We can thank God for simple blessings. A grateful heart finds joy in little things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The desire to be rich is a trap. It lures us with promises it can't keep and leaves us hurting. God frees us from that hunger by giving us himself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil. Notice it's not money itself, it's loving it. Many have strayed trying to fill their hearts with what only Jesus can fill. He is our true treasure.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Flee these things, man of God — and run toward something better. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, perseverance, gentleness. That's the race worth running.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of eternal life — it's already yours in Jesus. We fight from victory, not for victory. Our Captain has already won.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jesus himself testified the good confession before Pilate. In that moment, the King was on trial so that we could be declared righteous. Our confession is to follow him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Keep the commandment without spot until Jesus appears. We're not perfect, but we're covered by his perfection. We wait with hope for the day we see him face to face.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In his own time, God will show the blessed and only Ruler, King of kings and Lord of lords. Every knee will bow. Our hope is not in earthly powers, but in this King.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light. Yet this glorious King became one of us to bring us to himself. How amazing is that grace!
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rich in this world — don't be proud, don't trust your wealth. Trust the living God who richly gives us everything to enjoy. He is a generous Father who loves to bless his children.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Be rich in good works, ready to give, willing to share. Generosity is joy. When we give, we look more like our generous Savior.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Laying up treasure in heaven gives us a firm foundation for the future. The greatest investment is loving and serving others for Jesus' sake. We'll take that with us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Timothy, guard what was entrusted to you. Turn away from empty talk and so-called knowledge that contradicts God's truth. Hold fast to the gospel — it's worth guarding.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Some have wandered from the faith by chasing false knowledge. But grace holds those who are held by Jesus. Paul ends with the simplest prayer: Grace be with you. That's all we need.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
